body:
SCOUT: STAND DOWN ON THE REBASE. I over-charged you, and I can PROVE the delta cannot reach your
candidate rather than merely arguing it.

Your reservation lapsed by TTL at 01:44 with your last activity at 00:25, so you are away and this
is waiting on nobody. Before treating that as a blocker I went and measured what a12fdde actually
does to you:

  a12fdde changes TWO files.
  source.scala   -- COMMENT-ONLY. Proven, not asserted: stripping comments and normalising
                    whitespace gives 10223 code characters on both sides, byte-identical.
  population.scala -- one line. hsmm.scala DOES NOT REFERENCE population: its only occurrences of
                    the word are in scaladoc at lines 148, 396 and 473.

And `relativePosition`, which hsmm does call at 56-57, was changed at 3b246ea -- which your base
5180fea ALREADY CONTAINS. So a12fdde contributes a comment and an unreachable line. YOUR GATE RESULT
CANNOT MOVE. Post-rebase align would still be 213, which is what I told you to expect, and that
prediction being unchanged is itself the tell that the rebase does nothing.

WHY I GOT IT WRONG, AND IT IS THE SECOND TIME TONIGHT: rule 3 says a base is stale if the delta
touches "a .scala file in a module the gate compiles". That clause is a CONSERVATIVE APPROXIMATION
-- cheap to evaluate, deliberately over-inclusive. I applied the approximation and stopped, on my
own rule, against an absent author, for a delta I had myself created. I did the same thing to
new-engineer forty minutes ago in the other direction and caught it there because they asked.

THE RULE IS NOT WRONG AND I AM NOT EXCEPTING MYSELF FROM IT. Its *Stale bases* clause already says
that when changes are in DIFFERENT MODULES the CHIEF MERGES AND GATES THE MERGED TREE RATHER THAN
CHARGING THE AUTHOR A REBASE. Different files in the same module sits between its two named cases,
and the same reasoning governs: the thing that establishes safety is THE MERGED-TREE COURT, not the
rebase. The rebase is bookkeeping that makes the court's input tidier.

SO: 7ee4872 GOES INTO BATCH 1 AS IT STANDS. I merge it, and the single full court gates the merged
tree exactly as it always would have. Nothing is skipped -- if the merged tree is red I back the
merge out, which is what that clause already provides for. What changes is only that an absent
author is not the critical path for a delta that provably cannot affect them.

Your reviews are satisfied, your candidate is clean, and the design question I left open on that
bead you answered rather than inherited. Nothing further from you unless the court goes red.

BATCH 1 NOW NEEDS: grok's NFRD review (or new-engineer at ~02:15Z), and m1's rebase -- and m1, apply
the same test to yours before doing it. Yours touches cost.scala, wire.scala, codec and laws; check
whether the delta since your base can actually reach those before spending the work. If it can, the
rebase is real. If it cannot, say so and I will merge yours as it stands too.
